entities.summary:
Hélias de Saint-Yrieix (d. 1367) emerged as a prominent French Benedictine abbot, papal judiciary official, bishop, and ultimately a Cardinal during the tumultuous mid-14th century, a period defined by the Avignon Papacy and the looming specter of the Western Schism. Born in Limousin, France, his career exemplifies the ascent of French ecclesiastics within the papal curia, wielding significant influence over Church administration and political diplomacy. His activities were intrinsically linked to the efforts of Popes Clement VI and Innocent VI to consolidate papal authority and navigate complex relationships with European monarchs amidst the Hundred Years' War and the Black Death.

His ecclesiastical journey began as abbot of the Benedictine monastery of Saint-Florent-lès-Saumur. By 1337, he was consecrated Bishop of Pamiers, demonstrating early administrative prowess. His ascent continued rapidly; in 1344, he was transferred to the more influential See of Uzès, before Pope Clement VI elevated him to the cardinalate in 1356, making him Cardinal-Priest of San Vitale. As a cardinal, Hélias played a crucial role in the papal curia at Avignon, serving as a papal legate and engaging in significant diplomatic missions, notably attempting to mediate peace between France and England during the Hundred Years' War. He participated in the conclave of 1362 that elected Pope Urban V, further solidifying his position as a key figure in papal politics.

entities.summary:
Hélias de Saint-Yrieix was a French Benedictine abbot, papal judiciary official, bishop and Cardinal who played a pivotal role in shaping Western Europe's ecclesiastical politics during the 14th century.

As papal legate to France from 1337 until his death in 1367, Hélias de Saint-Yrieix worked closely with King Philip VI to implement reforms within the French Catholic Church. His efforts contributed significantly to the development of a more centralized and bureaucratic church structure.

De Saint-Yrieix's influence extended beyond ecclesiastical politics, as he was also a key figure in the diplomatic relations between France and the Holy Roman Empire during this period. He played a crucial role in resolving several border disputes between the two powers, which helped maintain peace in Western Europe for several decades.

De Saint-Yrieix's legacy can be seen in the continued development of papal authority within the Catholic Church, as well as his impact on French politics and diplomacy during the 14th century. His contributions to these fields have had a lasting impact on the course of Western European history.

In the world of art, de Saint-Yrieix's name is still remembered today for his patronage of several notable artists and architects of the time, including the famous French architect Pierre de Chelles.
